## Why This Is Asked
This question tests your ability to design an isolated audit pattern with in-cluster API access, RBAC scoping, and security boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped RBAC for fine-grained access control
- In-cluster API access using Secrets and ConfigMaps
- PVC-backed persistent logs and InitContainers for tooling
- NetworkPolicy for egress control to restrict traffic to the collector
- Health checks (readiness/liveness probes) for reliability

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: audit-baseline
  namespace: example
data:
  baseline.json: |
    {"pods": [], "services": []}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-auth
  namespace: example
type: Opaque
stringData:
  token: " collector-auth-token"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: audit-logs
  namespace: example
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: audit-agent
  namespace: example
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: audit-agent
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl jq && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
      containers:
      - name: auditor
        image: your-audit-image:latest
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while true; do audit.sh; sleep 60; done"]
        env:
        - name: COLLECTOR_URL
          value: "http://collector.audit-system.svc.cluster.local:8080"
        - name: AUTH_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: audit-auth
              key: token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
        - name: baseline
          mountPath: /baseline
          readOnly: true
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: audit-logs
      - name: tools
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: baseline
        configMap:
          name: audit-baseline
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-egress-restrict
  namespace: example
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: audit-system
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: collector
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **Pros**: Namespace isolation ensures audit agents don't interfere; NetworkPolicy provides security; PVC enables log persistence for compliance
- **Cons**: Each namespace requires separate Deployment (use Operator/Controller to automate); InitContainer adds startup latency; per-namespace RBAC management overhead increases with cluster size

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design an isolated TLS rotation workflow that leverages cert-manager, RBAC, and policy enforcement while producing auditable logs.

## Key Concepts
- Deployments, InitContainers, and probes for reliable pod lifecycle management
- Secrets and Bearer token authentication for secure credential handling
- cert-manager integration for automated certificate rotation testing
- PVC-based logging for persistent audit trails
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control and network segmentation

## Trade-offs
- **Simplicity vs. Security**: Using a single ServiceAccount with broad permissions simplifies implementation but increases blast radius if compromised
- **PVC vs. Sidecar**: A sidecar container offers simpler log shipping but adds resource overhead; a PVC requires external log rotation
- **Polling vs. Watching**: Polling with a cron-style schedule is less efficient than watching but avoids the complexity of setting up a custom controller with informers
- **Egress Control**: NetworkPolicy adds security but increases operational complexity and requires CNI support

  name: cert-verifier
---
apiVersion: v1

  name: cert-verifier
  namespace: cert-verifier

  name: cert-verifier
  namespace: cert-verifier

    resources: ["certificates"]
    verbs: ["get", "create", "delete"]

metadata:
  name: cert-verifier
  namespace: cert-verifier
subjects:

    namespace: cert-verifier
roleRef:

  name: cert-verifier
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-credentials
  namespace: cert-verifier
type: Opaque
stringData:
  token: "<bearer-token>"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier-logs
  namespace: cert-verifier
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:

metadata:
  name: cert-verifier
  namespace: cert-verifier
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cert-verifier
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cert-verifier
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: cert-verifier
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: alpine:latest
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - apk add --no-cache curl jq
          volumeMounts:
            - name: workdir
              mountPath: /work
      containers:
        - name: verifier

            - sh

            - name: workdir

            - name: logs

              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthy
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
        - name: workdir
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: cert-verifier-logs
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier-egress
  namespace: cert-verifier
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:

  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              name: audit-system
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: audit-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 443

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: data-qa-cronjob
  namespace: example
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: install-deps
            image: python:3.9-alpine
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              pip install pandas==1.3.3 jsonschema==3.2.0 --target /app/deps
            volumeMounts:
            - name: deps-volume
              mountPath: /app/deps
          containers:
          - name: validator
            image: python:3.9-alpine
            command:
            - python
            - -c
            - |
              import sys
              sys.path.append('/app/deps')
              import os
              import pandas as pd
              import jsonschema
              import requests
              from datetime import datetime
              
              schema_path = os.getenv('SCHEMA_PATH', '/data/schema.json')
              date_range = os.getenv('DATE_RANGE', '7')
              
              # Load schema
              with open(schema_path) as f:
                  schema = json.load(f)
              
              # Validate CSVs
              for csv_file in os.listdir('/data'):
                  if csv_file.endswith('.csv'):
                      df = pd.read_csv(f'/data/{csv_file}')
                      try:
                          jsonschema.validate(df.to_dict('records'), schema)
                          result = {'file': csv_file, 'status': 'pass', 'timestamp': datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}
                      except Exception as e:
                          result = {'file': csv_file, 'status': 'fail', 'error': str(e), 'timestamp': datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}
                      
                      # Send to QA portal
                      requests.post('http://qa-portal:8090/api/v1/qa', 
                                   json=result,
                                   headers={'Authorization': f"Bearer {os.getenv('QA_TOKEN')}"})

            - configMapRef:
                name: app-config
            - secretRef:
                name: qa-credentials
            volumeMounts:
            - name: data-volume
              mountPath: /data
            - name: deps-volume
              mountPath: /app/deps
              readOnly: true
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - python
                - -c
                - "import pandas, jsonschema, requests"
              initialDelaySeconds: 10
              periodSeconds: 5
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - python
                - -c
                - "import sys; sys.exit(0)"
              initialDelaySeconds: 30
              periodSeconds: 30
          - name: cert-rotator
            image: cert-manager/cert-manager-rotator:v1.8.0
            args:
            - --watch-cert-dir=/certs
            - --cert-secret-name=qa-tls-cert
            volumeMounts:
            - name: cert-volume

          volumes:
          - name: data-volume
            persistentVolumeClaim:

          - name: deps-volume

          - name: cert-volume

kind: ConfigMap

data:

## Trade-offs

**CronJob vs Deployment**: CronJob provides scheduled execution but lacks continuous monitoring. A Deployment could run continuously but would require external coordination.

**InitContainer Pattern**: Ensures dependencies are available but increases startup time and complexity. Using a pre-built image would be faster but reduces flexibility.

**Sidecar for TLS**: Separates concerns and enables independent updates but adds resource overhead and coordination complexity.

**NetworkPolicy Restriction**: Enhances security but requires careful rule management and monitoring to avoid blocking legitimate traffic.

**PVC for Data**: Ensures persistence across runs but creates coupling between namespaces and requires careful capacity planning.
